model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for several variants of a language model, including a baseline “Vanilla” model and multiple configurations of “StrmLLM” and “SepLLM” with different hyperparameters such as sequence length (n=64 or n=128) and the use of hierarchical or token-level processing (H, H/T). The x-axis, labeled “#Iteration,” spans from 0 to 140,000 with major tick marks every 20,000 iterations, using a linear scale. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” ranges from 2.4 to 3.4 with tick marks at 0.1 intervals, also on a linear scale. All lines begin near a loss of 3.4 at iteration 0 and exhibit a steep initial decline, followed by a slower, steady decrease toward convergence. The “Vanilla” model (purple, solid line) consistently achieves the lowest loss across iterations, ending near 2.5. The “StrmLLM (n=64)” (blue, solid) and “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” (red, solid) lines follow closely, ending around 2.55–2.6. The “SepLLM (n=64)” (orange, solid) and “SepLLM (n=64, H)” (green, solid) lines are nearly overlapping and slightly higher, ending near 2.6. The “SepLLM (n=128)” (dark blue, solid) line starts similarly but converges at a slightly higher loss (~2.65), indicating potentially slower or less effective optimization at the larger sequence length. All curves show smooth, monotonic decay with no visible oscillations or plateaus.
